subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private/VPC options, next steps
messages:
From: James Carter <j.carter@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lila Gomez <lila.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro & discovery call — quick recap

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful. I wanted to capture a short recap from our side and confirm the key constraints that will drive our decision.

High-level goals
- Replace our current rule-based document routing with a private LLM pipeline to classify and redact PHI.
- Keep inference on-prem / in our VPC (HIPAA + internal policy). No patient data should transit public L7 endpoints.
- Want a POC that demonstrates throughput at ~20 qps and avg latency <500ms for 1k-token chats.

Primary constraints / requirements you should know about
- Network: our subnet has strict egress controls. Any hosted control plane access must be via allowlisted IPs; we do not allow arbitrary outbound connections from the inference subnet.
- Data residency: all logs and model inputs must remain within our US region; audit logs need to be exportable to our Splunk instance.
- Air-gap: long-term preference is an air-gapped on-prem box for production; POC can be VPC-restricted.
- Security artifacts: we will need SOC 2 Type II, data flow diagrams, and KMS/HSM integration details.

Next steps from AcmeHealth
- I will route this to our InfoSec (Lila copied) and procurement. Procurement is aiming for a decision by end of June if the POC looks good.
- Please send a short list of network egress endpoints, any required ports, and a SOC2 stub.

Thanks — happy to jump on a security deep-dive next week if your team is available.

—James
James Carter
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
AcmeHealth

Happy to adjust timing; flag if Wed morning for the security call does not work.

Thanks James — quick tech note ahead of the security call with some practical options for the POC. High-level: we can support both a Redwood-managed private deployment (control plane in our managed account + customer VPC peering / private endpoints) or a customer-managed control plane deployed into your VPC/on-prem. Tradeoffs below.

Option A — Redwood-managed Private (fastest to start)
- Pros: fastest turnaround for POC (we provision dedicated instances and handle orchestration). Lower operational lift for Acme.
- Cons: Requires allowlisting a small set of Redwood control-plane IPs and an outbound path for control signals. No model/data egress from your subnet unless configured.
- Network asks: allowlist TCP 443 to: cp1.rw-inference.net (34.82.12.45), cp2.rw-inference.net (34.82.12.46). If you require IPs instead of DNS, we can provide a fixed set for the POC.

Option B — Customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem)
- Pros: full data residency, no outbound internet required from inference nodes (can be configured air-gapped for production).
- Cons: longer setup time; your infra team will handle upgrades and ops.
- Network asks: if you want a hybrid POC (control plane in your VPC but with reporting to Redwood), we only need intermittent egress for metrics; otherwise totally blocking egress is fine for an air-gapped install.

Security / compliance notes
- We support KMS integration and can integrate with customer-managed HSMs for key material.
- Audit logs: we can stream or export JSON logs to an S3-compatible endpoint or push to your Splunk via HTTPS forwarder.

Attachments
- redwood-private-deploy-pack.pdf (high-level deployment templates + firewall rules)

I’ll bring more detail to Wed’s call. If helpful, I can diagram a sample VPC peering + private endpoint flow before the meeting — ping me if you want that attached.

-David Kim
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
